blocks.task_summary: Show that p = -1 given that the vertex A of f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + p lies on the line y = 2x - 1.
method_path: Find x-coordinate of vertex A: x = -b/(2a) = -4/(2*(-1)) = 2
Substitute x = 2 into line equation y = 2x - 1 to get y = 3
Substitute x = 2 into f(x) = -x^2 + 4x + p, set equal to 3, solve for p: -4 + 8 + p = 3 => p = -1
accepted_alternatives: Find x-coordinate of vertex A = 2, substitute into f(x) to get f(2) = p + 4, set equal to 2(2)-1 = 3, solve p = -1.
Complete the square: f(x) = -(x-2)^2 + 4 + p, vertex A(2, 4+p), substitute into line: 4+p = 2(2)-1 => p = -1.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: x-coordinate of the vertex at A is 2 (A1); attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into equation of line (M1); 2(2)-1=3; 3 = -2^2 + 4(2) + p; p = -1 AG. METHOD 2: x-coordinate of the vertex at A is 2 (A1); attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into f(x) (M1); f(2) = p+4; p+4 = 2(2)-1; p = -1 AG. METHOD 3: attempt to complete the square on f(x) (M1); -(x-2)^2 + 4 + p; A x=2 OR A y=4+p (A1); 4+p = 2(2)-1; p = -1 AG.

blocks.task_summary: Find the value of q given that the vertex B of g(x) = x^2 + qx - 1 lies on the line y = 2x - 1.
method_path: Find x-coordinate of vertex B: x = -q/2
Substitute x = -q/2 into line equation y = 2x - 1 to get y = -q - 1
Substitute x = -q/2 into g(x) = x^2 + qx - 1, set equal to -q - 1, simplify to q^2 - 4q = 0
Solve quadratic: q(q - 4) = 0, discard q = 0 (non-zero constant), so q = 4
accepted_alternatives: Find x-coordinate of vertex B = -q/2, substitute into g(x) to get y = -q^2/4 - 1, set equal to 2(-q/2)-1 = -q-1, solve q^2 - 4q = 0, q = 4.
Complete the square: g(x) = (x + q/2)^2 - q^2/4 - 1, vertex B(-q/2, -q^2/4 - 1), substitute into line: -q^2/4 - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1 => q^2 - 4q = 0, q = 4.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: x-coordinate is -q/2 (A1); attempt to find intersection points, equating g(x) and 2x-1 (M1); x^2 + qx - 1 = 2x - 1; attempt to substitute their x-coordinate (M1); (-q/2)^2 + q(-q/2) - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1; q^2 - 4q = 0 (A1); q = 4 (since q ≠ 0) A1. METHOD 2: x-coordinate is -q/2 (A1); EITHER attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into y=2x-1 (M1); 2(-q/2)-1 => B(-q/2, -q-1); attempt to substitute their coordinates of B into g(x) (M1); -q-1 = (-q/2)^2 + q(-q/2) - 1; OR attempt to substitute their x-coordinate into g(x) (M1); (-q/2)^2 + q(-q/2) - 1 => B(-q/2, -q^2/4 - 1); attempt to substitute their coordinates of B into the line (M1); -q^2/4 - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1; THEN q^2 - 4q = 0 (A1); q = 4 (since q ≠ 0) A1. METHOD 3: attempt to complete the square on g(x) (M1); (x + q/2)^2 - q^2/4 - 1; B x = -q/2 OR y = -q^2/4 - 1 (A1); attempt to substitute their coordinates of B into equation of line (M1); -q^2/4 - 1 = 2(-q/2) - 1; q^2 - 4q = 0 (A1); q = 4 (since q ≠ 0) A1.
